scope: Eight exact Scryfall set codes from the remaining 21, with only the product-family claims actually supported by Wizards publications; no unsupported standalone/premier or format-legal claims.

grades.exact_code_and_group_primary: Wizards explicitly publishes set code and product group
grades.exact_product_primary: Wizards directly names the exact product, Scryfall establishes code
grades.product_family_primary_code_crosswalk_sc: Wizards directly supports the family and product components; dated Scryfall establishes code mapping, not asserted to be verified by Wizards

records.section: Sword of Dungeons & Dragons; HASCON card collaboration
records.detail: Wizards states that Sword of Dungeons & Dragons was included with other HASCON crossover promotional cards; H17 set code is independently sourced from the dated Scryfall catalog.
The Modern Horizons 2 Collector Boosters contain returning Modern Horizons cards in retro frames; H1R is a record of printings/treatments rather than a second MH1 launch.

records.section: Modern Horizons 3 Key Details — Retro Frame Reprints: H2R
records.detail: Wizards explicitly assigns H2R to 16 retro-frame reprints of Modern Horizons and Modern Horizons 2 included in MH3 products.

records.section: Gifts Given and Fruitcake Elemental — annual holiday gift cards
records.detail: Wizards describes the 2006 Fruitcake Elemental and 2007 Gifts Given as employee/business relationship holiday gift cards, not normal releases; HHO groups these archived holiday promo printings.
Wizards announced a limited charitable three-card silver-border My Little Pony product sold via Hasbro Pulse; not a main Magic draft booster.
Wizards describes 60 The List cards as traditional foil reprints found only in Unfinity Collector Boosters; ULST is not a separately published booster edition.

records.section: Playtest cards — Gavin Verhey Unknown events
records.detail: Wizards identifies special Unknown event card designs as playtests, some later receiving actual artwork in Mystery Booster 2; UNK records those event designs and does not imply a sold booster.

records.section: General Notes — W17 Welcome Deck ancillary product code
records.detail: Wizards explicitly identifies W17 as the code for Welcome Decks and other ancillary products that shared Ixalan-era constructed legality; these are introductory products, not separate expansions.
